status: STOPPED — the frozen generator cannot produce the study's required candidate pool
requirement: tools/s7/s7-scaling-preregistration.json (to be materialised) and the review brief: generate in frozen batches until there are at least 60,000 leakage-clean unique candidates, and at least 1.15x the calibration-predicted size of the largest 20x/16k arm (~46,600 rows)

measured.generator: cvslab.pool.selfplay, per-game RNG mode (generatorVersion 2), seed 20260920, 12 built-in opening lines, max_plies 70, sample_every 2, min_ply 6, play 20k nodes/move, diversification at plies (8,10,12) x 3 candidates within 25cp, diversification 2k nodes

disjoint_range_overlap.note: two game ranges 800 games apart produce almost the same positions

cause: the teacher is deterministic (cold fixed-node search), so play is a pure function of the start position except at the three diversification plies; the number of distinct game trajectories is therefore bounded by the declared opening source (12 lines) times the branching at plies 8/10/12, and the pool saturates at roughly 1.2k unique positions
consequence: the 20x/16k arm alone needs ~46,600 rows; the pool saturates three orders of magnitude short of that. No amount of additional generation reaches 60,000 with this opening source.

options.change: diversify play: sample among near-equal moves at every ply (or every N plies) instead of only plies 8/10/12 — a new generator contract (version 3)
options.yield_estimate: tens of thousands of unique positions; unverified
options.cost: generator change + verification, then ~20-40 min of parallel generation
options.scientific_effect: the pool becomes stochastic-play positions rather than deterministic-play positions; the S5/S6 pools' play contract is not preserved

options.change: start games from the engine's committed opening suite instead of the 12 hand-declared lines: benchmarks/suites/openings-inv1-20260910.epd, 4,910 positions, sha256 a477672523185ddc521e746de38b66bd253cade43488d640d43a0ec5175725dd
options.yield_estimate: ~4,900 start positions x ~33 sampled plies per game, mostly disjoint continuations: on the order of 100k+ raw rows and comfortably more than 60,000 unique candidates from one game per start position
options.cost: an opening-source loader + validation (~1 h), then ~20-30 min of parallel generation
options.scientific_effect: the generator contract is unchanged (deterministic cold play from a frozen, hashed start-position set); the start positions become Lichess-derived opening/middlegame positions (provenance file: harvested 2,300 positions from the app's lichess-dataset.jsonl, sha256 03410519..., filtered to fullmove 4-16, halfmove clock <= 6, material diff <= 2 pawns, >= 2 non-pawns per side, phases opening/middlegame), so the pool's distribution differs from the S5/S6 pools
options.note: the opening source is already a declared, hashed field of the pool config (openingSourceSha256), so this is a change of the declared source, not of the generator's semantics

options.change: take the candidate population from an existing corpus (e.g. the legacy gen9/gen10 shards or corpus-d20's ~43.4k unique positions) instead of generating one
options.yield_estimate: immediate, but corpus-d20 alone is below 46.6k + the 1.15x margin; corpus-static-full holds ~2.36M unique positions
options.cost: corpus selection + provenance + leakage join (the same machinery), no generation compute
options.scientific_effect: the pool is no longer fresh self-play; it is a legacy corpus with its own filters and provenance, which changes what the study's rows represent

recommendation_reason: it is the smallest change that reaches 60,000 candidates while keeping the frozen generator contract intact: only the declared opening source changes, and that source is a committed, hashed, provenance-documented engine artifact whose hash already travels in the pool manifest
